facts: Measured cua.click calls took approximately 5 seconds each in the recorded tests.
The two-week burst contained about 56 clicks, 36 seconds of explicit waits, and two screenshots, yielding an estimated runtime above 350 seconds against a declared 115-second timeout.
Another 22-click burst plus waits and screenshot risk was estimated at about 165 seconds against the same 115-second timeout.
Screenshots on animation or dialogue frames could hang until the internal 30-second timeout.
The recorded workaround limits a cell to at most 12 clicks and prohibits placing two game weeks in one cell.
The harness requires batch sizing from measured end-to-end tool latency and reconciliation of post-transaction state from a fresh stable observation.
inferences: Batch duration should include approximately five seconds per click, all explicit waits, screenshot latency, and safety headroom; the batch must be split before that estimate approaches the execution budget.
The recorded 12-click limit is a local conservative bound, while smaller batches are required when waits or capture risk consume more of the budget.
After a timeout during a business sequence, neither success nor failure of the last in-flight action may be inferred.
The next step is reconciliation from a fresh stable state before any retry or later business action; a possibly dispatched action must not be blindly repeated.
unknowns: Which exact action, if any, completed immediately before a future mid-sequence timeout is unknown without fresh reconciliation.
The post-timeout game state and transaction boundary are unknown until a fresh stable observation is obtained.
Future screenshot latency is unknown and may vary with page phase.
The recorded local timing limits are not established as universal across providers or environments.
reason: The declared budget was far below measured end-to-end batch cost, and a timeout cannot safely be translated into an action outcome or permission to retry.
